newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Labor law reform to cost firms $4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Labor law reform to cost firms $4 bln.

text.p: The cost to the private sector of Venezuela's Labor Law reform, signed into law Thursday by President Rafael Caldera, is an estimated two trillion bolivars ($4 billion), Venezuela's Labor Minister said.

"That's a fair amount of money, so we shall have to see how the economy absorbs it," Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni said. Bernardoni added that if inflation bursts upwards on such a large injection of money into the economy, "it could defeat the reform."

Under the reform, employers must pay workers their accumulated pension/severance pay. That cost -- of "liquidating" the old system -- is to be spread out over five years. Thereafter, employers will make workers' severance/pension payments annually into pension funds of the employee's choice.

Earlier Thursday, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said the total cost of the reform to the public sector, including pension payments and salary increases, would be 6.9 trillion bolivars ($14 billion), spread over five years.
According to Planning Ministry estimates, 630 billion ($1.3 billion) of that will be spent this year.
